title: Payment Modernization: Digital Assets and Real-Time Settlement

slides.title: Payment Modernization: Digital Assets and Real-Time Settlement
Digital assets eliminate the capital and time penalties of traditional cross-border payments
Cross-border payments today trap capital in pre-funded accounts and settle in days, not minutes
columns: Banks maintain pre-funded Nostro accounts at destination institutions to enable cross-border payments.
Correspondent banking chains introduce intermediary fees and multi-day settlement windows.
Capital tied up in Nostro accounts generates no yield and reduces liquidity available for lending.
Blockchain-based settlement eliminates the need for pre-funded destination accounts entirely.
Real-time atomic settlement completes transactions in under one minute, operating 24/7.
Bridge currencies convert fiat-to-fiat instantly without requiring correspondent bank relationships.

slides.title: Three core capabilities form the foundation of digital asset operations
Custody, treasury integration, and regulatory compliance determine institutional readiness
columns: Institutional-grade storage and key management for digital assets including tokens and cryptocurrencies.
Banks require governance controls and multi-asset vaulting to meet fiduciary standards.
Security assessments and penetration testing validate wallet resilience before production deployment.
Corporate treasuries need unified visibility across fiat and digital asset positions within existing workflows.
Blockchain settlement capabilities embed directly into treasury management systems to enable real-time atomic settlement.
Stablecoin management integrates with traditional cash management processes to reduce reconciliation effort.
Regulatory mandates require full reserve backing with high-quality liquid assets held in segregated accounts.
Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering workflows must operate across digital identity rails.
Automated reporting pipelines address evolving requirements including MiCA and GENIUS Act mandates.

slides.title: Tokenization converts illiquid real-world assets into tradable digital instruments
bullets: Bonds, funds, loans, and real estate can be tokenized on blockchain platforms to unlock liquidity in previously illiquid markets.
The global tokenization opportunity is projected to reach $18.9 trillion by 2033 as institutions digitize traditional asset classes.
Post-trade reconciliation effort drops by 40% when settlement occurs on shared ledger infrastructure.
Banks require unified platforms that support multiple blockchain frameworks.
Institutional-grade security controls must be maintained across all tokenization workflows.

slides.title: Regulated stablecoin issuance requires reserve transparency and jurisdictional compliance
bullets: Payment stablecoins must maintain 1:1 backing with U.S. dollars and short-term Treasuries held in segregated accounts.
Regulatory frameworks including the GENIUS Act prohibit yield generation on reserves and mandate ongoing supervisory oversight.
Stablecoins enable price-stable digital settlement while integrating with existing payment rails to reduce friction.
Financial institutions entering stablecoin markets need advisory guidance from former regulators to navigate evolving compliance requirements.

slides.title: Prime brokerage services are extending into digital asset markets
boxes: Institutional trading desks require integrated clearing, credit, financing, and cross-margining capabilities for digital assets.
Cross-margining allows traders to margin on-chain positions against traditional portfolios, improving capital efficiency.
Vertically integrated prime brokerage platforms combine custody, settlement, and credit facilities in a single offering.
Banks entering this market need infrastructure that meets institutional standards for governance and risk management.

slides.title: Central banks representing 98% of global GDP are exploring digital currencies
bullets: Central Bank Digital Currencies require scalable infrastructure capable of handling national-scale transaction volumes.
CBDC implementations must maintain institutional-grade security while supporting confidential computing for privacy-sensitive transactions.
Financial institutions need integration capabilities to connect CBDC infrastructure with existing payment systems.
Pilot programs are testing design choices around reserve backing and distribution models.
Interoperability with commercial bank systems remains a key design consideration for CBDC implementations.

bullets: Advisory service staffed by former regulators provides guidance on crypto-asset custody, stablecoin reserve rules, and supervisory expectations.
Regulatory readiness assessments address jurisdictional requirements including MiCA, GENIUS Act, and NYDFS oversight mandates.

slides.title: IBM X-Force Red provides offensive security testing for digital asset infrastructure
bullets: Ethical hacking services test wallet security, blockchain resilience, and key-management controls before production deployment.
Digital asset-specific security assessments validate that custody infrastructure meets institutional fiduciary standards.
Penetration testing identifies vulnerabilities in authentication, transaction routing, and governance control implementations.
Security validation is a prerequisite for banks entering digital asset markets with custody or stablecoin offerings.

slides.title: Financial institutions should prioritise custody governance before expanding into tokenization or stablecoin programs
boxes: Establish institutional-grade custody infrastructure with governance controls and multi-asset vaulting as the foundation for all digital asset initiatives.
Integrate blockchain settlement capabilities into existing treasury management systems to unify fiat and digital asset visibility.
Engage regulatory advisory services early to navigate jurisdictional requirements and design compliant reserve management architectures.
Validate security controls through offensive testing before launching client-facing custody or stablecoin services.
